audit.sourceAuditNotMeasured: Production input size validation, mutation receipts, details isolation, retained result budgeting and read-evidence projections have distinct semantics. Their repeated serialization was not proven redundant, and no guard or persistence view was removed.
audit.trustBoundaries: Thread counters observe each argument/result JSON string once, and instrument existing metadata JSON serialization sites without encoding them twice. They do not count V8/QuickJS internal copies or total heap allocations.
audit.productionDelta: No files under packages/ or tests/ changed. New production per-delta/progress/frame allocations are zero by unchanged source; existing runtime-call Promise/AbortController/message allocations are not claimed to be zero.
audit.lifecycle: Production ownership is unchanged. Diagnostic Worker subclass owns one 240-byte shared buffer per sampled execution; timestamp/counter arrays are read after termination, currentTrace is cleared, sandbox closes and builtin Worker exports restore in finally. Only numeric snapshots survive to the report. No disk temporary files or spawned services.
audit.poolDecision: No object or Worker pool. Timing attribution alone does not satisfy release/isolation/real-workload/profile gates.

gcInvestigation.initialObservation: Five GC calls in Promise continuations retained tool objects (indices 2/3 of 36); sandbox, catalog array, 30 results, controller and signal were collected. Same failure from source and compiled entry.
gcInvestigation.controls: Registration/no-op/tool-call and individual lifecycle probes released all references under Node 26.4.0 and Bun 1.4.0. The full measure sequence also released under a separate call site. This did not establish a production leak.
gcInvestigation.resolution: Only the GC probe changed: each of five Bun.gc(true) calls now runs in a native setImmediate callback instead of an async continuation. All 36 references release under source and compiled modes without clearing tool objects or weakening assertions. The exact JSC retainer mechanism is not established.
